types.meaning: One reusable ContextForge virtual server or native backend can serve many projects; project init binds the project or client to that existing service.
types.instantiation_rule: Instantiate once per canonical backend unless transport, credential, or safety boundaries prove another instance is needed.
readiness_evidence: target-client-visible list/call proof when a safe probe exists

types.meaning: Backend behavior depends on a provider credential, user account, installation, quota, or tenant boundary.
types.instantiation_rule: Instantiate per credential or user only when the backend cannot safely multiplex or when the credential boundary is the service boundary.
readiness_evidence: safe read-only target-client proof or explicit blocker

types.meaning: Backend behavior depends on a specific project root, code index, language server, cache, or project-local state.
types.instantiation_rule: Instantiate per project, or bind only to a previously approved project-specific instance.
readiness_evidence: target-client proof against the selected project instance

types.meaning: Backend behavior depends on an ephemeral client or session runtime such as a browser or shell/tmux session.
types.instantiation_rule: Instantiate per session/runtime boundary only when required by backend behavior.
readiness_evidence: explicit non-actions for unsafe runtime mutation

types.meaning: Service source lives in this repository and is stable, but calls may require an explicit repo argument or governance boundary.
types.instantiation_rule: Reuse the repo-local backend or transceiver; do not duplicate state into another source of truth.
readiness_evidence: read-only target-client proof that does not mutate repo ledgers

types.meaning: A user-home or container-user client hook, plugin, shim, or helper bootstrap that starts the project-init conversation; it is not itself a project service.
types.instantiation_rule: Install or seed per client user/home surface through its own approval path; project init must not silently write it.

types.meaning: A user-flow option such as None, skip, defer, or decline.
types.instantiation_rule: No backend, service binding, registry identity, or validation probe.

menu_examples.notes: Global documentation lookup scoped by tool arguments; first #260 single-service slice.
Provider-key, quota, cost, and redaction boundaries must be explicit before runtime proof.
GitHub account/token boundary; read-only proof only unless a later issue approves writes.
Repo-local governance MCP; validation must list/read governance only and must not mutate ledgers.
Remote native template/documentation service; safe proof is constrained preview generation only.
Isolated browser runtime; proof must use a controlled fixture page.
Existing-session visibility only; no opening sessions or sending commands without separate approval.
Provider/request scoped; safe low-cost query only after credential and redaction boundaries are bounded.
Project-specific code intelligence; provisioning and language choice remain explicit approval boundaries.
Covered by decline/defer flow, not service readiness.

mapping_rules: Client configs are consumption surfaces, not service identity.
Service binding suffixes such as canonical or credential_scoped are stable identifiers; taxonomy_type is the authoritative lifecycle/localization class.
Project-local activation may bind to a shared service without creating a per-project backend.
User-global hooks and helper bootstraps trigger or facilitate initialization but are not selected project services.
Credential-scoped services must not claim readiness from token or host-auth presence alone.
Project-scoped services must not activate another project's backend unless compatibility is explicitly documented and validated.
Session-scoped services must not use unsafe side effects as ordinary validation proof.
Backend health, bridge checks, and registry readback can support lower readiness layers, but target-client readiness requires target-client surface evidence.
